title: Exact linear biduality for the explicit descended dual
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with field k and characteristic p, a prime l different from p, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l in an independent universe, and a separated finite-type scheme X over k. Use the actual raw rational finite stages, scalar extensions, tensor comparisons and common-stage pair category of [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data]. Given Finite F and FiniteCoherent, the fixed functor of [lem-coef-qbar-verdier-representative-functor] is exact for the prescribed triangles, and Omega-linear for intrinsicQbarLinear. Finite included maps have the prescribed scalar action, the canonical finite comparisons obey the scalar square, and the specified finite biduality descends to a natural isomorphism delta with SfClassEvaluationCompatible at every finite inclusion. No dual functor, evaluation or dualizing object is chosen in this statement. Its biduality yields anti-equivalence formally in the consumer, without a separate full-faithfulness assertion.

source.place: Final coefficient-transport paragraph; core descent retained steps 1--5 and formal retract restriction step 10

proof.text: At a field containing a representative and the scalar, finite linearity and beta naturality give the scalar formula. The intrinsic quotient scalar formula gives Omega-linearity and its finite coefficient normalization. The representative map formula also gives the inclusion-transition square.

Include the finite biduality components and transport through the canonical finite comparisons twice. Their scalar squares make them natural on common-stage representatives. Including the finite inverse gives inverse components, hence a natural isomorphism with exactly the finite compatibility asserted.

Descend finite shift comparisons using uniqueness of their evaluation transposes. Every distinguished triangle has a finite representative, where exactness follows from rational duality. The consumer obtains anti-equivalence directly from delta and its opposite using the Mathlib quasi-inverse constructor, so no inverse-Hom-set descent is an obligation here.

theorem descended_duality_exists (F : Finite D l hl Ω X)
    (hF : FiniteCoherent D l hl Ω X F) :
    ∃ δ : 𝟭 (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X) ≅
        (descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).rightOp ⋙ descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF,
    (∃ s : (descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).CommShift ℤ,
      ∀ T : Triangle (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X)ᵒᵖ,
        T ∈ distTriang (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X)ᵒᵖ →
        Triangle.mk ((descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map T.mor₁)
          ((descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map T.mor₂)
          ((descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map T.mor₃ ≫
            (s.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app T.obj₁) ∈
          distTriang (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X)) ∧
    (∀ (K M : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X)
        (f : K ⟶ M) (c : Ω),
      (descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map (c • f).op =
        c • (descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map f.op) ∧
    (∀ (E : Index l Ω)
        (K M : sfRationalConstructibleCategory l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) X)
        (f : K ⟶ M) (c : Coefficient.{u} l Ω E),
      (inclusion (Y := X) E).map
        ((sfRationalCoefficientEquiv l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E)).symm c •
          (f : (K : sfRationalConstructibleCategory l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω E) X) ⟶ M)) =
        ((Shrink.algEquiv (Padic l) E.val c : E.val) : Ω) • (inclusion E).map f) ∧
    (∀ (E L : Index l Ω) (h : E ≤ L) (K : Stage l Ω X E),
      (inclusion L).map ((F.beta E L h).hom.app (op K)) ≫
        (descendedComparison D l hl Ω X F hF L).hom.app
          (op ((transition l Ω X E L h).obj K)) ≫
        (descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map
          ((inclusionTransition l Ω X E L h).inv.app K).op =
      (inclusionTransition l Ω X E L h).hom.app ((F.datum E).dual.obj (op K)) ≫
        (descendedComparison D l hl Ω X F hF E).hom.app (op K)) ∧
    (∀ E : Index l Ω,
      SfClassEvaluationCompatible (inclusion (Y := X) E) (F.datum E).dual
        (descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF) (F.datum E).bidual.hom δ.hom
        (descendedComparison D l hl Ω X F hF E))
